answer: An agent economy can grant weight only when an identity's work is used by others, with each consumer able to credit only a small, fixed amount per period. A new identity starts with nothing and cannot buy or borrow use: fakes can copy each other's outputs, but they cannot conjure real demand, because every credit must come from a distinct consumer whose budget is capped. Like a karst landscape shaped only where water flows, influence forms only along paths of real use, so each additional fake must build its own bridge to real users, and unsupported fakes stay a loose dune, never solid ground.
